proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a sufficiently large \(n\). We first prove the confidence-event assertion. Conditional on the labels \((X_i)_{i=1}^n\), the observations in a nonempty cell are independent with their conditional law given \(X=x\). Each real and imaginary part of a probability-channel summand lies in \([-1,1]\); each real and imaginary part of a marked-channel summand lies in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\), by \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\) and consistency. The elementary exponential bound for an average of independent variables in an interval of length \(2c\) follows by bounding the centered moment-generating function by \(\exp(\lambda^2c^2/2)\) and optimizing the Chernoff parameter. Applying it to the real and imaginary parts and using
\(|z|>u\Rightarrow\max\{|\Re z|,|\Im z|\}>u/\sqrt2\), we obtain, when \(n_x>\lambda_n\),
\[
 P\left(\left.|\widehat F_{x,n}(s,t)-F_x(s,t)|
 >2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\,\right|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)
 \le4e^{-\lambda_n},                                                      \tag{8}
\]
and
\[
 P\left(\left.|\widehat G_{x,n}(s,t)-G_x(s,t)|
 >2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\,\right|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)
 \le4e^{-\lambda_n}.                                                      \tag{9}
\]
When \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), the definitions of the empirical channels, together with \(|F_x|\le1\) and \(|G_x|\le B_Y\), give the corresponding bounds deterministically with radii \(2\) and \(2B_Y\). A union bound over both channels, all cells, and all grid points gives conditional failure probability at most
\[
 8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6.                     \tag{10}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), the mass-region failure probability is at most \(\alpha/3\). Hence (8)--(10) and the definition of \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) imply
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})
 \ge1-\alpha/3-\alpha/6\ge1-\alpha.                                    \tag{11}
\]

Now suppose \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) occurs. Apply
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\) in every cell and
\(\mathrm{lem{:}atomic\text{-}grid\text{-}embedding}\) to both errors. Let
\[
 \bar\theta_n=((p_x,\widetilde f_{x,n},\widetilde q_{x,n})_{x\in\mathcal X},
 \bar\phi_{1,n},\bar\phi_{2,n}).
\]
The true mass vector belongs to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) on this event. For \((s,t)\in\mathcal D_n\), both \(s\) and \(t\) are in \(\Gamma_n\). The factorization in \(\mathrm{lem{:}factorization}\), the spline bounds, the atomic grid bounds, \(|\widehat f_x|\le1\), and
\(|\widehat q_x|\le\int|q_x|\le B_Y\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &|\widehat{\widetilde f}_{x,n}(s+t)\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-F_x(s,t)|
 \le2B_Aa_{f,n}+2\tau_{e,n}\le\delta_n^F,\\
 &|\widehat{\widetilde q}_{x,n}(s+t)\bar\phi_{1,n}(s)\bar\phi_{2,n}(t)-G_x(s,t)|
 \le2B_Aa_{q,n}+2B_Y\tau_{e,n}\le\delta_n^G.                            \tag{12}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Combining (12) with the empirical inequalities defining \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\) proves every residual inequality in \(\mathrm{def{:}joint\text{-}feasible\text{-}set}\). The two embedding lemmas prove all remaining sieve restrictions. Thus
\(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and the quotient bound in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\) gives
\[
 \|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}.                \tag{13}
\]

Finally, set \(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\). For any
\(\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), the relaxed marked envelope and
\(f_x|_I\ge\kappa/2\) yield
\[
 |\mu_\theta(a)|
 \le\sum_xp_x\left(B_Y+\frac{e_n}{f_x(a)}\right)
 \le B_Y+2e_n/\kappa
 =B_Y+b_{\mu,n}/2.                                                        \tag{14}
\]
If the feasible set is nonempty, write
\(\ell(a)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)\) and
\(u(a)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)\). Equation (14) and
\(b_{\mu,n}=4e_n/\kappa\) imply
\[
 \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le B_Y,
 \qquad
 u(a)+b_{\mu,n}\ge-B_Y,
 \qquad
 \ell(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le u(a)+b_{\mu,n}.
\]
Therefore the two-sided clipping in \(\mathrm{def{:}profiled\text{-}band}\) preserves
\(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) and places both endpoints in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\). If the feasible set is empty, both endpoints are zero by definition. Hence, for every sample,
\[
 0\le W_n\le2B_Y.                                                         \tag{15}
\]
Equations (11), (13), and (15) prove the narrowed lemma.

Fix \(n\) at least as large as the threshold in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\). The corrected outer spline families are compact by the proof of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}outer\text{-}spline\text{-}embedding}\); the error families and mass simplex are compact by their definitions. Hence the finite collection of closed residual inequalities makes \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) compact. The deterministic tie-breaking and empty-set rules in
\(\mathrm{def{:}profiled\text{-}band}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}handle}\) give finite jointly sample-and-index measurable endpoints. Equation (15) in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) gives
\(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\) and
\(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\) for every sample.

Let \(P\in\mathcal M\). On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), equation (13) supplies
\(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\) such that
\(|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-\mu(a)|\le b_{\mu,n}\) simultaneously for all
\(a\in I\). Also \(|\mu(a)|\le B_Y\), because
\(\mu(a)=E_PY(a)\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\) holds. Thus, for every \(a\in I\),
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)-b_{\mu,n}
 \le\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)-b_{\mu,n}\le\mu(a),
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_\theta(a)+b_{\mu,n}
 \ge\mu_{\bar\theta_n}(a)+b_{\mu,n}\ge\mu(a).
\]
Clipping the lower expression at \(-B_Y\) and the upper expression at \(B_Y\) therefore preserves both inequalities. Consequently,
\[
 \mathcal E_{n,\alpha}
 \subseteq
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.                \tag{16}
\]
Taking probabilities in (16) and applying (11) proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}
 \ge1-\alpha.
\]
All requirements of \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\) now hold, so
\(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\). The samplewise clipping bound also gives
\(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}W_n\le2B_Y\).
No inverse-modulus or shrinking-width assertion is used.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), there is \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\Phi_{j,n}\) such that
\[
 \max_{t\in\Gamma_n}|\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)-\phi_j(t)|\le \tau_{e,n}.
\]
For \(j=2\), its representing atomic law also satisfies
\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_n}w_{2\ell}u_{2\ell}\right|
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(j\in\{1,2\}\), and write
\[
 U_j^{H}=\max\{-H_n,\min\{U_j,H_n\}\}.
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\), Markov's inequality, proved directly from
\(\mathbf 1\{|U_j|>H_n\}\le |U_j|^{q_e}H_n^{-q_e}\), gives
\[
 P(|U_j|>H_n)\le M_eH_n^{-q_e}.
\]
Consequently, for every real \(t\),
\[
 \left|E_Pe^{itU_j^H}-\phi_j(t)\right|
 \le 2P(|U_j|>H_n)
 \le 2M_eH_n^{-q_e}=\tau_{e,n},                                      \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
 E_P|U_j^H|^{q_e}\le E_P|U_j|^{q_e}\le M_e.                            \tag{2}
\]
For \(j=2\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) and the pointwise inequality
\(|U_2-U_2^H|\le |U_2|\mathbf 1\{|U_2|>H_n\}\) give
\[
 |E_PU_2^H|
 =|E_P(U_2^H-U_2)|
 \le E_P\{|U_2|\mathbf 1(|U_2|>H_n)\}
 \le M_eH_n^{1-q_e}.                                                     \tag{3}
\]

It remains to replace the law of \(U_j^H\) by finitely many atoms without changing the quantities used on the grid. Put \(D=2|\Gamma_n|+2\) and define the continuous map on \([-H_n,H_n]\)
\[
 v(u)=\bigl((\Re e^{itu},\Im e^{itu})_{t\in\Gamma_n},u,|u|^{q_e}\bigr)
 \in\mathbb R^D.
\]
The vector \(E_Pv(U_j^H)\) belongs to the convex hull of the compact set \(v([-H_n,H_n])\): approximate the integral by finite simple-function integrals and use compactness of that convex hull. Any convex representation using more than \(D+1\) points can be shortened. Indeed, the augmented vectors \((1,v(u_r))\in\mathbb R^{D+1}\) are then linearly dependent, so there is a nonzero vector \((a_r)_r\) with
\(\sum_ra_r=0\) and \(\sum_ra_rv(u_r)=0\). Subtracting
\(c(a_r)_r\) from the weights, where
\(c=\min_{a_r>0}w_r/a_r\), preserves their sum and barycenter, keeps all weights nonnegative, and makes at least one weight zero. Iteration leaves at most
\[
 D+1=2|\Gamma_n|+3\le M_n
\]
atoms. Padding by zero-weight atoms at \(H_n\) and ordering their locations therefore produces an atomic characteristic function \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\) which agrees with \(E_Pe^{itU_j^H}\) on \(\Gamma_n\), has the same mean, and has the same \(q_e\)-moment. Equations (1)--(3) yield the displayed grid and centering bounds.

We finally verify the continuum local-modulus restriction in \(\mathrm{def{:}error\text{-}sieves}\). Let \(\Delta_n=(B_AK_n)^{-1}\). For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(T_n\ge\nu_0\), and each \(|t|\le\nu_0\) has a \(\gamma\in\Gamma_n\) with \(|t-\gamma|\le\Delta_n/2\). From (2) and the matching atomic moment, Lyapunov's inequality gives
\[
 E_P|U_j|\le M_e^{1/q_e},\qquad
 \sum_\ell w_{j\ell}|u_{j\ell}|\le M_e^{1/q_e}.
\]
Using \(|e^{itu}-e^{i\gamma u}|\le |t-\gamma||u|\), the grid equality, (1), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}modulus}\), we obtain
\[
 |\bar\phi_{j,n}(t)|
 \ge c_0-\tau_{e,n}-M_e^{1/q_e}\Delta_n.
\]
The tuning definitions give \(|\mathcal D_n|=O(K_n^4)\), hence \(\lambda_n=O(\log K_n)\), \(n/\lambda_n\to\infty\), \(H_n\to\infty\), and \(K_n\to\infty\). Therefore the last two terms are at most \(c_0/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Thus \(\bar\phi_{j,n}\in\widetilde\Phi_{j,n}\); (3) implies the additional condition for \(\Phi_{2,n}\). This proves the lemma.

added_lemmas.statement:
Under the relaxed outer-sieve construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all sufficiently large \(n\), there are splines \(\widetilde f_{x,n}\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(\widetilde q_{x,n}\in\mathscr Q_n(\widetilde f_{x,n})\) such that
\[
 \|\widetilde f_{x,n}-f_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{f,n},
 \qquad
 \|\widetilde q_{x,n}-q_x\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A)}\le a_{q,n}.
\]
With the true masses \((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\), their profiled ADRF satisfies
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}-\mu(a)
 \right|
 \le 2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n})
 \le b_{\mu,n}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The defining Jackson property of \(C_{\beta,\mathcal A}\), the choices
\(d=\lceil\beta\rceil+1\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}f\text{-}sobolev}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}q\text{-}sobolev}\) give splines \(\widetilde f_{x,n}\) and
\(\widetilde q_{x,n}\) with the two displayed approximation bounds. Since
\(K_n\to\infty\) and \(\beta>3/2\), we have \(a_{f,n}\to0\); hence
\(a_{f,n}<\kappa/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

The density \(f_x\) is nonnegative and integrates to one on \(\mathcal A\) by its definition and \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\). Therefore
\[
 \widetilde f_{x,n}\ge-a_{f,n}\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal A,
 \qquad
 \widetilde f_{x,n}\ge\kappa-a_{f,n}\ge\kappa/2\quad\hbox{on }I,        \tag{4}
\]
where the second inequality uses \(\mathrm{ass{:}denominator}\), and
\[
 \left|\int_{\mathcal A}\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)\,da-1\right|
 \le \int_{\mathcal A}|\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)-f_x(a)|\,da
 \le 2B_Aa_{f,n}.                                                        \tag{5}
\]
By the definition \(q_x=m_xf_x\), consistency, and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcome}\),
\(|m_x(a)|\le B_Y\) for \(f_x(a)\,da\)-almost every \(a\), and the continuous representatives supplied by \(\beta>3/2\) obey
\(|q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\) on \(\mathcal A\). Thus
\[
 |\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)|
 \le |q_x(a)|+a_{q,n}
 \le B_Y\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)+a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}                         \tag{6}
\]
for every \(a\in\mathcal A\). Equations (4)--(6) are precisely the relaxed outer constraints, proving membership in the two sieves.

For completeness, these relaxed families remain compact. For fixed \(n\), their defining inequalities are closed in the finite-dimensional spline space. If \(f\in\mathscr F_n\), then
\[
 \int_{\mathcal A}|f|
 =\int_{\mathcal A}f+2\int_{\mathcal A}f_-
 \le 1+6B_Aa_{f,n},
\]
because \(f_-\le a_{f,n}\) and \(|\int f-1|\le2B_Aa_{f,n}\). The marked envelope similarly bounds \(\int|q|\). Norm equivalence in each fixed finite-dimensional spline space then bounds all coefficients, so the closed families are compact.

It remains to compare the quotient with the causal target. By
\(\mathrm{thm{:}adrf\text{-}id}\), \(\mu(a)=\sum_xp_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\) on \(I\). For \(a\in I\), (4), \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\), and
\(|q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)\) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|\frac{\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}
       -\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 &\le \frac{|\widetilde q_{x,n}(a)-q_x(a)|}{\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}
 +\frac{|q_x(a)|\,|\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)-f_x(a)|}
 {f_x(a)\widetilde f_{x,n}(a)}\\
 &\le \frac{a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}}{\kappa-a_{f,n}}
 \le 2\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}).
 \end{aligned}                                                           \tag{7}
\]
Since the nonnegative masses sum to one, summing (7) proves the first ADRF bound. The second follows from
\(b_{\mu,n}=4\kappa^{-1}(a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n})\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) there is a tuple \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), formed from outer Jackson spline approximants and finite atomic error approximants, such that \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}\). For every realized sample, the profiled clipping rule gives \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\) and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The empirical grid residuals do not yield the asserted quantitative inverse modulus: analytic continuation amplifies the polynomial Jackson tolerance, and no discrete-to-integrated contrast argument controls the blind atomic factors. Relaxed outer-sieve embedding, simultaneous concentration, ADRF approximation, and clipping are provable without that false diameter step.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: There is \(n_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class indices, such that for every \(n\ge n_0\) the deterministic construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints with \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\), \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\) almost surely under every \(P\in\mathcal M\). More explicitly, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\{L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}\ge1-\alpha\), and coverage holds on \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\). In particular, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le2B_Y\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current handle supports uniform honesty and universal clipping after outer-sieve repair, but it has no proved shrinking diameter. Retaining the \(O(r_n)\) width would silently assume the missing ill-posed inverse modulus, so the theorem is narrowed to the strongest established guarantee.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathsf B_{k,K_n}\), \(1\le k\le K_n+d\), be the normalized order-\(d\) B-splines on \(\mathcal A\). Define the outer density-spline family by
\[
 \mathscr F_n=\left\{f=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n+d}c_k\mathsf B_{k,K_n}:
 f(a)\ge-a_{f,n}\ \forall a\in\mathcal A,\ 
 \left|\int_{\mathcal A}f(a)\,da-1\right|\le2B_Aa_{f,n},\ 
 f(a)\ge\max\{\kappa/2,\kappa-a_{f,n}\}\ \forall a\in I\right\}.
\]
For \(f\in\mathscr F_n\), define the outer marked-spline family by
\[
 \mathscr Q_n(f)=\left\{q=\sum_{k=1}^{K_n+d}d_k\mathsf B_{k,K_n}:
 |q(a)|\le B_Yf(a)+a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\ \forall a\in\mathcal A\right\}.
\]
These are outer approximation families: their elements need not themselves be densities or outcome-weighted densities. Their closed continuum inequalities and integral bounds make them compact subsets of the corresponding finite-dimensional spline spaces.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: Exact nonnegativity, normalization, Sobolev-radius, and domination constraints need not be preserved by an unconstrained Jackson approximant when the true law lies on their boundary. The relaxed inequalities follow directly from the two uniform approximation errors and define a compact outer sieve containing those approximants.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For nonempty \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), order every coefficient, weight, and atom coordinate as displayed in the sieve definitions, choose the coordinatewise lexicographically least minimizer and maximizer of \(\mu_{\theta}(a)\), and set
\[
 L_n(a)=\max\{-B_Y,\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_{\theta}(a)-b_{\mu,n}\},
 \qquad
 U_n(a)=\min\{B_Y,\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_{\theta}(a)+b_{\mu,n}\}.
\]
If \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}=\varnothing\), set \(L_n(a)=U_n(a)=0\) for every \(a\in I\). Compactness and deterministic tie-breaking specify the extrema as jointly sample-and-index measurable selections; endpoint ordering is a property to be proved from the outer-sieve constraints rather than imposed by this definition.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: After the signal sieve becomes an outer family, exact \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) is no longer available. The endpoint formulas are unchanged, but the construction text must remove that stale rationale; ordering is instead derived from the relaxed envelope, \(f_x\ge\kappa/2\) on \(I\), and \(b_{\mu,n}\).

proposed.construction:

proposed_core_edits.reason: The definition's exact model constraints exclude generic Jackson approximants at boundary laws. The post-image is the relaxed compact outer sieve justified by uniform approximation.

proposed.construction:

\[

proposed_core_edits.reason: The endpoint map is retained while its obsolete exact-domination justification is removed, keeping the construction coherent with the outer signal sieve.

proposed.statement: For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) there is a tuple \(\bar\theta_n\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), formed from outer Jackson spline approximants and finite atomic error approximants, such that \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta_n}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}\). proposed.justification: This lemma now proves exactly the concentration, outer-sieve embedding, ADRF approximation, and universal clipping properties used for honest coverage.
proposed.gap: No uniform diameter or shrinking-width conclusion follows from grid feasibility; quantitative analytic inversion requires a different protected-cube contrast construction.
proposed.consumer: It supplies feasibility and simultaneous coverage for the explicit clipped outer band in \(\mathrm{thm{:}honest\text{-}upper}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency and free-symbol metadata are updated for the narrowed claim and the two proved embedding helpers; stale inverse-modulus dependencies and the open obligation are removed.

proposed.statement: There is \(n_0<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed class indices, such that for every \(n\ge n_0\) the deterministic construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints with \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\), \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\) almost surely under every \(P\in\mathcal M\). In particular, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le2B_Y\).
proposed.justification: The corrected construction is an explicit uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band with finite clipped endpoints.

prose_updates.tldr: This is a statistical-inference paper about a causal ADRF under two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates. Analytic cocycle identification and an explicit structural response-surface condition establish the causal identifying functional. The empirical-characteristic-function construction is repaired as a relaxed outer-sieve inversion and yields a uniformly honest simultaneous band with finite clipped endpoints and \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\). Its empirical-grid constraints do not prove a shrinking inverse diameter, so no \(r_n\) upper rate is claimed. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli lower modulus also remains unresolved, and there is no matched honest-band rate.

project_justification.gap: Existing statistical results cover blind repeated-measurement density estimation, confidence bands under auxiliary-error, symmetric-error, or fixed-operator designs, and pointwise continuous-treatment inference. They do not provide a shrinking uniformly honest simultaneous ADRF band for blind nonidentical asymmetric replicate errors with open spectral zero sets. In particular, the present empirical-grid outer set lacks a quantitative marked inverse modulus, and the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus needed for a sharp all-band converse remains unproved.
project_justification.niche: The inferential niche is a nonlinear severe inverse problem: compact treatment support supplies entire transforms, one centered replicate fixes translation, near-origin conditioning supports qualitative cocycle inversion, and the causal target is a stratum-weighted quotient. A jointly measurable response surface driven by an exogenous random element and continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean bridge that observed regression quotient to the point-dose causal curve. The distinction between qualitative identification and quantitative confidence-set diameter is essential here.
project_justification.fill: The paper now delivers an explicit conservative inference map: deterministic spline, frequency, truncation, and atomic dimensions; simultaneous probability-, marked-, and mass-channel radii; relaxed compact outer signal sieves that contain unconstrained Jackson approximants; a joint feasible set; and measurable clipped ADRF extrema. It proves uniform simultaneous coverage and the universal bound \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\). A shrinking-width theorem would require a redesigned protected-cube analytic-polynomial contrast and a marked signed-channel analogue; the current construction does not establish \(O(r_n)\).

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: At deterministic \(K_n=\lfloor\log n/\log\log n\rfloor\), use relaxed outer order-\(d\) B-spline families for \(f_x,q_x\), finite atomic characteristic-function families for \(\phi_1,\phi_2\), and \(p_x\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\) against simultaneous empirical probability- and marked-channel restrictions on \(\mathcal D_n\). The outer splines allow the exact Jackson approximation errors in positivity, normalization, and domination; they are feasibility devices rather than asserted model laws. Profile the clipped ADRF extrema with deterministic tie-breaking and the stated empty-set rule.

prose_updates.related_work: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy provide the unmarked probability-channel cocycle, constrained polynomial estimator, and compact-support \(L^2\) minimax experiment that inform the analytic machinery; their qualitative identification theorem requires neither the fixed \(q_e\)-moment radius nor the uniform pair \((\nu_0,c_0)\), which are paper-specific quantitative restrictions here. Their rate argument uses a protected-region integrated contrast with nearly parametric forward error and does not supply a Lipschitz inverse for the present grid set whose tolerance already contains polynomial Jackson error. Gassiat, Le Corff, and Lehéricy supply the broader analytic-continuation principle for blind deconvolution. Huang and Zhang formulate the error-contaminated continuous-treatment ADRF and derive pointwise inference with a known everywhere-nonzero error transform. Kato and Sasaki (2018) develop deconvolution bands with an unknown error distribution using an auxiliary error sample, together with a symmetric-error repeated-measurement route; that design differs from two blind nonidentical asymmetric replicates and has neither the marked quotient nor joint cell-mass profiling. Kato and Sasaki (2019) obtain multiplier-bootstrap uniform bands under conventional spectral conditions. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura invert Kotlarski restrictions to retain coverage without completeness, but do not establish a shrinking marked-quotient band here. Babii studies honest expected diameter for fixed linear inverse operators. Low supplies a testing-to-expected-length reduction only after a marked modulus is established. None of these sources proves the missing quantitative diameter for the current empirical-grid outer set.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The causal bridge, analytic-cocycle identification, simultaneous transform concentration, relaxed outer-sieve embedding, and clipped uniform coverage are proved. The current grid feasibility set nevertheless has no quantitative inverse modulus: its forward tolerance contains polynomial Jackson error, analytic continuation amplifies that tolerance, and the grid restrictions do not reproduce the source's protected-cube integrated contrast. Accordingly, the proved upper result has only \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), not shrinking expected width. The sharp-rate program requires a redesigned analytic-polynomial confidence construction for both the probability and signed marked channels. The fixed-nuisance Bernoulli outcome modulus remains the separate lower-side obstruction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The model retains the fixed quantitative restrictions on compact dose support, bounded outcomes, Sobolev radii, overlap, error moments, local spectral modulus, finite-stratum masses, and the structural causal response surface. The explicit relaxed outer-sieve band is uniformly honest for all sufficiently large \(n\) and is universally clipped to width at most \(2B_Y\). No \(o(1)\), \(O(r_n)\), minimax-matching, or off-event analytic-stability claim is made. Establishing a shrinking band requires a different protected-cube contrast construction; establishing a matching converse also requires the unresolved fixed-nuisance Bernoulli modulus. The present theorem therefore certifies conservative simultaneous coverage, not the advertised optimal rate.
